conviction_note: A mild positive lean, not a call. Peer and industry evidence (Munich Re's Q3 pre-release, which beat consensus by 15% with major losses below budget; global insured cat losses for 9M26 at the lowest since 2019) points to a Q3 above the EUR 638m consensus and makes a raise of the 2026 floor (at least EUR 2.7bn, against a polled consensus of EUR 2.77bn) plausible. Against that: the stock ran up 10.9% in 20 days on exactly this read, JPMorgan's downgrade to Underweight hit it on 6 Nov, the soft cycle (Swiss Re 9M P&C revenue and new-business CSM down) is the line the market trades, and this name sold its last two beats (Q1 2026 -2.6%, H1 -0.2%). The 2027 first guide, which drove the prior two Q3 days (+3.1%, +3.5%), is reported to come at the 25 Nov Investors' Day, outside the window. So abs_move is 4.0 (new numbers plus a possible guide change) and p_up is only 56. The findings sum to +1.0 and the scaled number is +0.48: same sign, and the gap is p_up's pull toward 50.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 was a benign catastrophe quarter for reinsurers: 9M26 global insured nat cat losses were about USD 92bn, the lowest since 2019, and Munich Re pre-released Q3 at about EUR 1.7bn against a EUR 1.479bn consensus with P&C reinsurance major losses below expectations. That points to a Hannover Q3 above the EUR 638m consensus (-2% y/y), and the EUR 590m investment-result estimate looks low against H1's run-rate of about EUR 650m a quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name sells profit beats. Q1 2026 (11 May, net income +48%) fell 2.62%, and H1 2026 (12 Aug, large losses under budget) fell 0.16%, both computed from Yahoo daily closes.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the 20-day run-up is +10.9%, and the Munich Re ad-hoc is two weeks old. The consensus of EUR 638m (-2% y/y) has not moved up with it, which suggests the sell-side numbers were not refreshed for the benign quarter. If they had been, the Q3 estimate would sit above Q3 2025's EUR 651m. Hannover's method of booking the full large-loss budget damps how much of the under-run reaches net income, so this is sized small.
findings.independence: Gallagher Re's 9M26 cat report via Artemis (https://www.artemis.bm/news/gallagher-re-estimates-global-insured-cat-losses-at-92bn-for-9m26-lowest-since-2019/, 2026-10-21) is an independent industry series. Hannover's own Monte Carlo release (7 Sep) also says nat cat losses were 'moderate on the whole so far this year'.

findings.finding: The 2026 guide looks too low against the run-rate: H1 already delivered EUR 1.4bn (52% of the 'at least EUR 2.7bn' floor) with large losses EUR 240m under budget, Q3 was benign, Munich Re raised its target on the same facts, and Hannover itself raised at Q3 2025 (from about EUR 2.4bn to about EUR 2.6bn). A raise toward about EUR 2.8-2.9bn is the likely release line, against a polled consensus of EUR 2.77bn.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 (10 Nov 2025): guide raised and 2026 guide introduced, stock +3.54%. FY2025 results (12 Mar 2026): +4.45%. Both from Yahoo closes; dates from the issuer's EQS archive.
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus of EUR 2.77bn sits only 2.6% above the floor, so the market expects a firming more than a raise. The German preview says outright 'Ob der Rückversicherer den Ausblick anhebt, ist offen' ('Whether the reinsurer raises its outlook is open'). A raise to EUR 2.9bn would land above consensus. If that were priced, consensus would already sit near EUR 2.9bn. Offset: Hurricane Isaias in Q4 (9 Oct) and Hannover's habit of conservatism could keep the guide at 'at least 2.7bn'.
findings.independence: Precedent: the 9M25 release raised the 2025 guide (https://www.eqs-news.com/news/corporate/hannover-re-raises-earnings-guidance-for-2025-after-very-good-business-performance/12c1c277-1a35-490c-8187-d52f5facb20d_en). Munich Re's raise is a separate document but rests on the same benign-cat fact as the finding above, so it is partly shared.

findings.finding: The soft cycle is landing in the numbers peers have just printed. Swiss Re's 9M26 P&C Re net income fell 6% on competitive conditions, with P&C revenue and new-business CSM down sharply. Hannover's own H1 new-business CSM was already -13.3% and traditional P&C revenue only +0.2% FX-adjusted. So the Q3 revenue estimate (EUR 6.6bn, +4%) and the renewal commentary are the downside lines.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H1 2026 (12 Aug), when new-business CSM fell 13.3% alongside a profit beat: -0.16%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the JPMorgan downgrade on the same thesis took the sector down 4%+ on 6 Nov, before the entry. What is left is whether Hannover's Q3 revenue misses the +4% consensus, which the company's own H1 data (traditional P&C +0.2% FX-adjusted) make plausible. If it were fully priced, the revenue consensus would not be at +4%.
findings.independence: Hannover's own H1 statement (new-business CSM -13.3%; 1 June/1 July renewal prices -4.5%), https://www.eqs-news.com/news/corporate/hannover-re-generates-very-good-half-year-result-and-remains-on-track-to-achieve-full-year-guidance/7f35e761-e745-4bd8-8612-f782110a766e_en

findings.finding: The bar was reset lower the session before the window. JPMorgan cut HNR1 to Underweight (target EUR 270) on valuation, 2027 price pressure and the reserve buffer relative to earnings, and the stock fell about 4.8% intraday on 6 Nov alongside Munich Re -4.2%, Swiss Re -4.6% and the DAX -2.6%. The entry price therefore already holds a fresh bear case, and the release's reserve-buffer commentary is the line that can rebut it.
findings.original_quote: „Der Analyst verweist darauf, dass der Reservepuffer zwar wieder aufgebaut wurde, gemessen an der erwarteten Ertragskraft aber nicht so kräftig sei wie in früheren Phasen.“ (The analyst notes that the reserve buffer has been rebuilt, but measured against expected earnings power it is not as strong as in earlier phases.)
findings.why_not_priced: The downgrade itself is priced at entry. The open question is whether the release (Hannover routinely reports its reserve resilience) answers the reserve critique. A sector-wide one-day drop of this size with the DAX -2.6% is partly market beta, and the next session can recover part of it. A small inference, sized small.

baseline_tension: The positive Q3 and guide read agrees with the +10.9% 20-day run-up, which is why it is sized small; the priced lean is -0.54 (from the run-up) and JPMorgan's downgrade on the eve of the print pulls the other way. language_note: German preview copy (ad-hoc-news.de, goldesel.de, both 6 Nov) carried the company-polled consensus: Q3 net income EUR 638m, investment result EUR 590m, revenue EUR 6.617bn, FY EUR 2.77bn, combined ratio 85.3%. The English searches returned no Q3 consensus at all.
German copy carried the expectation that the 2027 target comes at the end-of-November Investors' Day and not on 9 Nov; this cut abs_move and moved the largest historical swing line out of the window.
The German write-ups of the JPMorgan note carried its reserve-buffer argument verbatim, which sets the release line the stock can trade on.
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' and 'you were right about the number and too small about the move': abs_move_pct raised from 3.3 to 4.0, since the quarter is new and a 2026 guide change is plausible; the guidance finding raised from +0.6 to +0.8, sized on the guidance scale.
'Two findings resting on one document are one finding': the Q3 read-through shares the benign-cat fact with the guide finding, so it was cut from +0.6 to +0.4 rather than counted twice.
'A verified fact is not a predicted reaction' (this name sold its Q1 and H1 beats): p_up moved from 57 to 56.
'A German ad-hoc filed before the print may have pre-released the number': checked, none filed, so the quarter is genuinely new.
'Keep findings inside the exit window': the 2027 guide stays in outside_window (Investors' Day on 25 Nov).
